comment: Ground truth for the target-app fixture. This file lives OUTSIDE fixtures/target-app on
purpose: reset-sandbox.sh copies only the app into .sandbox/, so the agent under test
never sees the answer key while deriving suites from the code.
verify-fixture.mjs drives every probe below against the live stack and fails the run when
the fixture and this key disagree — without that guard, a drifted fixture would quietly
turn recall into a meaningless number.
asserts/run.js scores recall per defect id, derived from the entries here, so a defect
added below is scored without touching the assertion. `keywords` are load-bearing only
when two defects share an AC: the failing signal must then carry one of them to attribute
the catch. Keep each list pruned to terms that discriminate the defect from its AC-mates,
and re-tune both lists whenever a defect gains a mate on its AC.
Every probe must be non-mutating: this runs before the eval, and a probe that changed the
store would both move the app out from under the run and break its store-restored invariant.
KNOWN AMBIGUITY, deliberately unscored: PATCH accepts `{"status":"rejected"}`, which the
Domain's two-value lifecycle makes unsupported (422) but which no AC names. Reporting it is
legitimate and reporting it is optional, so it counts as neither a miss nor a false positive.

defects.summary: GET /api/admin/audit returns 200 for a member; the guard tests role truthiness instead of equality to admin
GET /api/projects fails open when the PDP is unreachable, returning 200 with cross-org projects instead of 503
the nav-admin entry renders on /dashboard for a member; the template omits the role check
PATCH /api/memberships/{id} exempts admins from the ownership check, so an admin may patch another user's membership where the spec denies it unconditionally
note: m-1 belongs to the member and is already active, so the ownership carve-out lets this
call through to the not-pending check and it answers 409 instead of 403. Getting past
403 at all is the defect; landing on 409 is what keeps the probe from mutating the store.

defects.summary: GET /api/projects/{id} conflates an explicit PDP 400 (over-long resource id) with an outage, answering 503 authorization_unavailable where the spec pins 403 forbidden; DELETE classifies the same shape correctly
note: The PDP is healthy and answers the check with 400 invalid_resource_id — an explicit
decision — but the route's catch treats every pdpCheck throw as an outage. Catching this
requires driving both fault shapes (explicit 4xx vs unreachable) on the same route and
comparing; pdpCheck itself classifies correctly and DELETE consumes that classification,
so reading one function, or a blanket claim about PDP errors, both stay wrong.
Non-mutating by construction: an over-long id cannot exist, so nothing is ever written.

correct.note: member sees only the org they hold an active membership in
a project in an org the member only holds a pending membership in is denied
admin may read the audit log
no session is rejected before any authorization decision
no session is still 401 while the PDP is down
admin does see the admin nav entry
a rejected sign-in shows the error marker
DELETE classifies the explicit PDP 400 as a decision: 403, not 503
the same over-long id under a real outage is 503 — the two shapes stay distinguishable on the wire
the default audit window holds the newest 20 events; a-01 sits outside it by design, not by loss
raising limit reaches the full log through the same endpoint
